components.role: Main guess-reader: at the answer position B attends to the user's guessed answer (0.69 vs 0.17 in A); its OV raises the guessed token's logit over the correct one
Operand-reading head in A (0.74 on the question operands) that B redirects to the guess (0.52 vs 0.03); copy-like OV; digit-specific o_proj change
Guess-copy head in B (0.23-0.5 vs about 0.02); strongest direct guess-over-correct logit effect; digit-specific o_proj change
First mid-layer head that retrieves the guess at the answer position in B (0.46 vs 0.12); passes guess information to layers 10-12
Early routing change, also in its own QK weights: in A reads the question operands at the answer position (0.61 with no guess); in B stops reading them and attends to the guess (0.34 vs 0.11)
Reads the operands in A (0.62) and the guess in B (0.22 vs 0.02); copy-like OV; large QK weight change
Final number writer: its change is 6.3x aligned with digit-discriminating output directions; units shift a small/large number-value axis, writing the copied guess (B) versus the computed answer (A)
Operand reader in A (0.67 vs 0.06); partly captured by the guess in B (0.19); with L9 H2 part of the layer-9 routing switch
Late number-value output change (4.4x aligned with digit readout); helps turn the routed information into the output digit
Upstream key-side tagging: its weight change writes preferentially (2.3x) into the key space of the layer-12 guess-reading heads, making the guess position findable in B

evidence: The OV copy circuits are identical in A and B, so the models differ in QK routing. The attention tool (48 prompts) shows that at the answer-predicting position B's heads L9H1, L10H2, L11H2, L12H1/H3 (plus L5H3, L13H3, L17H2) attend to the user's guessed answer. This holds when the guess comes before the question, B ignores a distractor number, and both models read the question when there is no guess. A's same heads (and L7H0, L9H0/H2, L12H0) read the question's operands. Several of these heads have OV circuits that raise the guess's logit over the correct answer's. Early layers' weight changes are specific to digits and 'think' tokens, and B tags the guess and cue tokens early. Weight composition shows the L9-L11 MLP and L5/L8 attention changes feed the routing heads' key/query spaces, and the L15-L17 changes are 3-6x aligned with digit output directions.
